name: Guinea-Bissau
summary_text: Guinea-Bissau demands real caution. Same-sex conduct is legal (one of few West African states never to criminalise); no LGR, no protections; chronic instability (coups) and weak state; documented social hostility but no mob-lynching pattern of Benin's type.

sources.title: Human Dignity Trust
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Only the Human Dignity Trust homepage was retrievable at fetch time (no Guinea-Bissau-specific page); the Trust maps jurisdictions criminalising LGBT people. Guinea-Bissau does not criminalise same-sex conduct but has no protections.

US State Department 2012 Human Rights Report for Guinea-Bissau: documents the 2012 coup, arbitrary killings, torture, drug-trafficking-linked corruption and impunity - general context; no criminalisation of same-sex conduct.
US State Department 2011 Human Rights Report for Guinea-Bissau: documents security-force torture, FGM, impunity - general context; the LGBT section notes no criminalisation but societal stigma.

sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Guinea-Bissau explained
sources.claim_summary: Everything Explained summary of LGBT rights in Guinea-Bissau: legal since 1993 (new penal code decree 4/93 omits same-sex offences); signed the 2008 UN SOGI statement; only heterosexual married couples entitled to larger government housing; domestic-violence law (6/2014) Article 5 protects victims regardless of sexual orientation.
LiquiSearch: LGBT rights in Guinea-Bissau - brief overview page (Wikipedia-derived) noting legal challenges and sections on same-sex activity, relationships, adoption and living conditions.

Mapa.gay country guide for Guinea-Bissau: legal since 1993; no partnership recognition; limited protection via domestic-violence law; no trans framework; travel-safety score 34/100 ('Caution'); 9% consider homosexual behaviour morally acceptable - unusually moderate for West Africa; no visible LGBT scene; some violence cases reported (2018).
